items.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
items.one_liner: An actively exploited OS command injection flaw in Zimbra has been added to CISA's KEV, requiring immediate patching.

items.title: Hackers infect Android car head units with proxy botnet malware
items.one_liner: Supply-chain attack on Android car infotainment systems turns vehicles into proxy botnet nodes.
items.summary: A supply-chain attack targeting Android-based car head units from Chinese provider DoFun is using a legitimate update app (TWCore) to distribute "JarService" malware. Attributed to the MoYu group, the malware enlists devices into a proxy botnet (using the 'zhima' module) or performs ad fraud via click-fraud activity. While it does not affect critical driving systems, it provides attackers with shell-level access and the ability to execute arbitrary code.
items.bottom_line: Android-based car head units are being compromised via legitimate update channels to serve as residential proxy nodes for cybercriminals.

claims.text: A supply-chain attack on Android car head units uses a legitimate update app to spread malware.
claims.support_span: A supply-chain attack targeting Android-based car head units is using a legitimate device-update app to spread malware that enlists compromised devices in a proxy botnet or uses them for ad fraud.

claims.text: The malware turns the head unit into a proxy botnet node using a module named 'zhima'.
claims.support_span: Researchers discovered that the operator primarily loaded a reverse-proxy module named ‘zhima,’ which turns the head unit into a proxy botnet node

items.title: Microsoft Patches Severe Entra ID Flaw (CVSS 10.0) Allowing Remote Code Execution
items.one_liner: Microsoft patched a CVSS 10.0 deserialization RCE flaw in Entra ID (CVE-2026-69836), confirming no active exploitation.
items.summary: Microsoft disclosed and addressed a maximum-severity remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-69836, CVSS 10.0) in its cloud identity service Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD). The flaw stems from untrusted data deserialization, permitting unauthenticated attackers to execute remote code over the network. Although initial advisories erroneously stated active in-the-wild exploitation, Microsoft clarified that the issue was identified internally by Robert Fitzpatrick and was patched without requiring customer action. The service mitigation has been deployed across cloud infrastructure.
key_facts: CVE-2026-69836: CVSS 10.0, Remote Code Execution via Untrusted Deserialization
Affected service: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory)
Exploitation status: Not exploited in the wild (corrected)
items.bottom_line: Microsoft has resolved a critical CVSS 10.0 RCE flaw in Entra ID on the backend, requiring no tenant-side patching actions.

items.title: MalSkills: Detecting Malicious Skills in the Agentic Supply Chain via Neuro-symbolic Reasoning
items.one_liner: Essential reading for anyone using third-party "skills" or plugins in their LLM agent workflows.
items.summary: MalSkills is a neuro-symbolic framework designed to detect malicious modules (skills) in the agentic supply chain. It combines symbolic parsing with LLM-assisted semantic analysis to extract security-sensitive operations and construct a skill dependency graph. By reasoning over this graph, it can identify suspicious workflows that traditional static or dynamic analysis might miss. In a real-world scan of over 150,000 skills from public registries, MalSkills flagged 620 potentially malicious items, 400 of which were confirmed as malicious.
items.bottom_line: Automated neuro-symbolic analysis has successfully identified hundreds of malicious packages in public LLM agent registries, proving the reality of agentic supply chain attacks.

items.title: Connecting the Dots: Securing the Overlooked Corners of the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) Supply Chain
items.one_liner: The ChainDrop npm worm highlights how attackers poison CI/CD pipelines and developer environments to harvest cloud secrets and propagate malware.
items.summary: Recent threat intelligence from Unit 42 highlights a massive shift in supply-chain attacks toward poisoning the software development lifecycle (SDLC) rather than targeting finished applications. A notable example is the ChainDrop npm worm, which infected over 400 packages—including keyv and cacheable-request—using a stealthy three-step chain involving modified preinstall hooks and the Bun runtime. The worm reads live process memory from GitHub Actions runners to harvest temporary OpenID Connect (OIDC) tokens and credentials, backdoors developer tools like VS Code, and uses Ethereum blockchain transactions for dynamic command-and-control communication. Because modern applications are assembled from thousands of indirect open-source dependencies, these attacks compromise developer laptops, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud environments before code ever reaches production.
items.bottom_line: The ChainDrop worm infected over 400 npm packages by exploiting preinstall scripts to harvest GitHub Actions tokens and backdoor developer environments.

items.one_liner: A critical RCE in widely used Citrix NetScaler gateways requires immediate patching of SAML-configured appliances.
items.summary: watchTowr Labs has analyzed a Heap Overflow vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway that allows for Remote Code Execution (RCE). items.title: CSS:the bomb inside your inbox
items.one_liner: A PortSwigger study reveals how webmail CSS/HTML sanitizer flaws and label element abuses allow UI hijacking and token theft.
items.summary: Gareth Heyes from PortSwigger Research published a study on how webmail clients render untrusted CSS and HTML, exposing vulnerabilities where sanitization can be bypassed. The research highlights how HTML label elements with the 'for' attribute can inherit click actions on form elements to hijack user interfaces, control UI ribbons, and pin messages without user consent. Tested across clients like Yahoo Mail, AOL Mail, Fastmail, ProtonMail, Gmail, and Outlook, the findings demonstrate that sanitizers frequently fail to filter dangerous attributes properly. The bugs allow attackers to break trust boundaries, exfiltrate tokens, compromise third-party sites, and execute indirect prompt injections in AI-enabled mail clients.
key_facts: Affected targets: Yahoo Mail, AOL Mail, Fastmail, ProtonMail, GMail, Outlook, OpenAI Atlas
items.bottom_line: Webmail sanitizers that fail to strip the 'for' attribute from label elements let malicious emails inherit form clicks and control user interfaces.

items.title: CRLF-Powered Desync Attacks: Beheading HTTP Streams
items.one_liner: An advanced research paper details how Nginx proxy_pass CRLF normalization enables HTTP desync worms and browser-based cookie theft.
items.summary: PortSwigger Research published a paper co-authored with Tobia Righi exploring CRLF-powered HTTP header injection primitives that transform into desync worms, IP-locked desyncs, and browser-based XSS attacks. The research demonstrates how Nginx normalizes the uri variable in proxy_pass directives by url-decoding characters like %0d%0a, allowing attackers to inject new lines and take full control of forwarded requests upstream. By bypassing cross-network restrictions through the victim's browser, the technique can steal HTTPOnly cookies and generate out-of-thin-air XSS. The authors present these findings to warn against underestimated header injection vulnerabilities and help defenders avoid accidental desync disasters.
key_facts: Authors: PortSwigger Research and Tobia Righi (TurtleSec)
Vulnerability type: CRLF-Powered Desync Worm / HTTP Header Injection
items.bottom_line: Nginx proxy_pass configurations that include the unencoded $uri variable allow attackers to inject CRLF sequences and achieve request smuggling and desync attacks.

claims.text: In Nginx configurations (an extremely popular web server) if the $uri variable is included in the proxy_pass directive, Nginx will normalise the request path before use, url-decoding any encoded characters including CRLF sequences (%0d%0a).

items.title: Rapid7 Analysis: Microsoft SharePoint Remote Code Execution (CVE-2026-63520)
items.one_liner: Rapid7 published an analysis of SharePoint CVE-2026-63520, showing how malicious .bdcm files enable .NET type instantiation and RCE.
items.summary: Rapid7 and Microsoft disclosed CVE-2026-63520, an RCE vulnerability in Microsoft SharePoint's Business Data Connectivity (BDC) subsystem caused by unrestricted .NET type instantiation and property setting in the DbTypeReflector class. An authenticated attacker can upload a malicious .bdcm model file to instantiate arbitrary assembly-qualified types from the Global Assembly Cache and achieve OS command execution. When chained with authentication bypass CVE-2026-55040, the flaw results in unauthenticated remote code execution. Because third-party details of the vulnerability were published prematurely, Rapid7 expedited its technical analysis documenting gadget chain construction via ObjectDataProvider.
key_facts: Affected Software: Microsoft SharePoint Server Subscription Edition version 16.0.19725.20210
Component: Business Data Connectivity (BDC) subsystem (DbTypeReflector class)
items.bottom_line: CVE-2026-63520 allows authenticated attackers to achieve RCE via unsafe .NET type resolution in SharePoint's BDC subsystem, becoming unauthenticated when chained with CVE-2026-55040.
